config.title: JWT Storage & Decode in React

intro.title: JWT Storage & Decode in React
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React application that securely stores a JSON Web Token (JWT) in the browser's localStorage and decodes it to display user information. You will learn the core concept of handling authentication tokens in a client-side application, including storage and data extraction. The main technologies involved are React hooks like useState and useEffect, the localStorage API, and the jwt-decode library. By the end, you'll understand how to manage user sessions by safely storing tokens and accessing their payload data without sending them to a server.
intro.usecase: In real-world React applications, JWT storage and decoding is essential for user authentication and authorization. When users log into platforms like e-commerce sites, banking dashboards, or project management tools, their JWT tokens are stored locally to maintain sessions. Developers decode these tokens to display user-specific content, such as personalized dashboards, role-based navigation menus, or secure payment forms. This pattern ensures secure, persistent user experiences without requiring constant re-authentication.

objectives: Implement secure JWT storage in React using localStorage
Construct a function to decode JWT tokens and extract payload data
Apply conditional rendering based on authentication state from JWT
Initialize authentication state by retrieving stored JWT on component mount
Integrate JWT decoding with protected route components
Manipulate JWT data to display user information in the UI
Configure token validation by checking expiration timestamps
Control authentication flow by clearing JWT tokens on logout

steps.title: Import React, useState, and useEffect
steps.instruction: Import React, useState, and useEffect from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the hooks you'll need for state and side effects.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and hooks
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React, useState, and useEffect here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary imports are added to the file.
successCriteria: React, useState, and useEffect are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import all three: React, useState, and useEffect from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import React, useState, and useEffect from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty React fragment for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called App that returns <> </>.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: A component named App is created and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named exactly 'App' and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named App that returns <> </>.

steps.title: Initialize state for JWT token
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'token' initialized to an empty string.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty string as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into 'token' and 'setToken'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a state variable
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a token state variable ready to store a JWT string.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an empty string, and the returned array is destructured into 'token' and 'setToken'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using useState with an empty string and destructuring the array into 'token' and 'setToken'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'token' initialized to an empty string.

steps.title: Initialize state for decoded token data
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use useState to create a state variable named 'decodedData' and initialize it to null.
steps.hint: Add a new useState call similar to your token state, but with the variable name 'decodedData' and initial value null.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a state variable for user data
const [userData, setUserData] = useState(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two state variables: one for the raw JWT token and another for the decoded payload data.
successCriteria: The App component contains a 'decodedData' state variable initialized to null using useState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to create a variable named 'decodedData' with initial value null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the useState call for 'decodedData' inside the App component with initial value null.

steps.title: Create handler to store JWT in localStorage
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a function named 'storeToken' that takes a token parameter and saves it to localStorage with the key 'jwtToken'.
steps.hint: Use localStorage.setItem('jwtToken', token) inside the function body.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a storeToken function that can persist JWT tokens to the browser's localStorage.
successCriteria: The storeToken function is defined, takes a token parameter, and calls localStorage.setItem('jwtToken', token).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your storeToken function takes a token parameter and uses localStorage.setItem with 'jwtToken' as the key.
steps.feedbackWrong: The storeToken function should save tokens to localStorage. Try creating a function that accepts a token and uses localStorage.setItem('jwtToken', token).

steps.title: Create handler to decode JWT payload
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'decodeToken' that takes a JWT token string as a parameter and returns the decoded payload object.
steps.hint: You'll need to split the token string by '.' to access the payload part, then decode it from base64 using atob().
steps.expectedOutcome: A decodeToken function that extracts and parses the payload from a JWT token string.
successCriteria: The decodeToken function is defined, takes a token parameter, splits it correctly, decodes the payload using atob(), and returns the parsed JSON object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the decodeToken function, but make sure it properly splits the token, decodes the base64 payload, and returns the parsed JSON object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The decodeToken function isn't implemented correctly. Remember: JWT tokens have three parts separated by dots, and the payload needs base64 decoding.

steps.title: Add useEffect to load token on component mount
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, add a useEffect hook that calls the getStoredToken function and sets the token state when the component first mounts.
steps.hint: Use useEffect with an empty dependency array to run only on mount. Call getStoredToken inside the effect and use setToken to update the state with the retrieved token.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook is added with an empty dependency array, calling getStoredToken and updating the token state on component mount.
successCriteria: The useEffect hook is defined with an empty dependency array and contains a call to getStoredToken and setToken.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your useEffect has an empty dependency array and calls both getStoredToken and setToken.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useEffect hook is missing or doesn't match the requirements. Remember to use useEffect with empty dependencies to run on mount, call getStoredToken, and update the token state.

steps.title: Add input field for entering JWT token
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a text input element with a placeholder attribute set to 'Enter JWT token here'.
steps.hint: Use the <input> JSX element with type='text' and placeholder='Enter JWT token here'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: adding a text input
<input type="text" placeholder="Enter your name" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now render a text input field where users can type JWT tokens.
successCriteria: The return statement contains an <input> element with type='text' and placeholder='Enter JWT token here'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the input field for JWT token entry.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the input has both type='text' and placeholder='Enter JWT token here' attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field is missing or incorrect. Add <input type="text" placeholder="Enter JWT token here" /> inside the return statement.

steps.title: Add store button and wire to storeToken handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Store Token' inside the div. Set its onClick handler to call storeToken with the current token state value.
steps.hint: Create a button element with onClick={() => storeToken(token)}. The button text should be 'Store Token'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button with click handler
<button onClick={() => handleClick(value)}>Click Me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Store Token' appears in the UI. When clicked, it will call the storeToken function with the current token value.
successCriteria: The button element is present with text 'Store Token' and has an onClick handler that calls storeToken with the token state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but check that it calls storeToken with the token value when clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly wired to the storeToken handler.

steps.title: Add decode button and wire to decodeToken handler
steps.instruction: Add a button labeled 'Decode Token' in the return statement, with an onClick handler that calls the decodeToken function.
steps.hint: Place the button after the existing store button. Use the onClick attribute to call decodeToken when clicked.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click Me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Decode Token' appears in the UI, which when clicked will trigger the decodeToken function.
successCriteria: Button element with text 'Decode Token' and onClick attribute set to call decodeToken.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but check the label text or onClick handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly configured.

steps.title: Display decoded token data
steps.instruction: In the return statement of your App component, add a section below the decode button that displays the decodedData state in a readable format using JSON.stringify.
steps.hint: You can use a <div> or <pre> element to display the data. The decodedData state is already defined - just render it with JSON.stringify(decodedData, null, 2) for pretty formatting.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying data in React

Decoded Data:

{JSON.stringify(userData, null, 2)}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a section that displays the decoded JWT payload data in a formatted JSON structure when the decode button is clicked.
successCriteria: The return statement includes an element that renders decodedData using JSON.stringify
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying the decodedData state using JSON.stringify for proper formatting.
steps.feedbackWrong: The decoded data section isn't displaying correctly. Check that you're rendering the decodedData state with JSON.stringify in the return statement.
